links.outcome: Alignment of LLM confidence with accuracy under linguistic uncertainty and missing information
links.effect: Accuracy degraded with increasing uncertainty while confidence stayed misaligned with accuracy, causing a substantial increase in unsafe confident errors (UCER).
links.quote: Our results reveal a consistent failure mode, i.e., although accuracy degrades under increasing uncertainty, model confidence remains misaligned with accuracy.

links.outcome: Ability of LLMs to abstain when the correct answer option was removed
links.effect: Significant variation across models in abstaining when the correct answer is unavailable; some models persistently produced high-confidence hallucinated answers.
links.quote: Furthermore, we observe significant variation across models in their ability to abstain when the correct answer is unavailable, with some models persistently producing high confidence hallucinated answers.

unlisted_practices: Uncertainty-aware evaluation using calibration gap, ECE, and Unsafe Confident Error Rate before clinical deployment

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating LLM overconfidence and failure to abstain under uncertainty using the MedMCQA dataset; it does not test a health system deployment practice or safeguard.
